summary: The charging-case lid is one of the most frequently handled parts of a TWS product. Hinge clearance, magnet placement, shell flatness, opening angle, sound and surface finish shape the perceived quality before the earbuds are even used. This iSoud guide helps private label buyers define charging-case lid and hinge expectations without relying on vague premium-feel language.

sections.title: Why a small hinge gap is not the only quality measure
body: Huawei support guidance explains that charging-case lids are connected by a hinge and that slight movement or sound can occur during opening, closing or pressing. Xiaomi support guidance similarly notes that a reasonable hinge gap can be needed for smooth opening and closing. These examples show why buyers should define function and allowable variation rather than demand a visually zero gap.

A private label project should review hinge geometry, lid-to-body alignment, magnet closure, opening force, maximum angle, side play, sound and surface appearance as one system. Tightening one dimension without reviewing the full assembly can create rubbing, poor closure or inconsistent feel.

sections.title: Charging-case hinge RFQ questions for an OEM/ODM factory
bullets: What hinge structure, pin material and assembly method are used in the selected case?
Which lid-to-body gaps and alignment differences are visually acceptable?
How are opening force, closing force, magnet pull and maximum opening angle checked?
Does the lid remain stable in the intended open position during normal earbud removal?
Which sounds, looseness, rubbing marks or surface defects cause rejection?
How many open-close cycles are used for development or production validation?
Are hinge and lid checks repeated after custom paint, coating, printing or shell changes?

sections.title: Magnet feel, shell tolerances and hinge alignment interact
body: Sennheiser's charging-case overview identifies magnetic earbud holders, charging compartments and charging contacts as integrated case features. In a compact case, the lid magnets, earbud magnets, hinge and molded pockets all compete for space and must remain aligned with the final shell parts.

The signed sample should record the hinge parts, magnets, shell material, coating, assembly method and approved feel. A custom finish can change friction or reveal rubbing at the split line, while altered magnet position can change closure behavior.
bullets: Inspect the split line from front, side and rear views.
Compare opening and closing with earbuds present and removed.
Check lid stability at normal one-handed opening angles.
Look for coating wear near hinge and magnet-contact areas.
Retain approved sound and feel references with dimensional samples.

sections.title: Cycle testing needs buyer-defined acceptance criteria
body: A cycle count has little value without before-and-after checks. Buyers can define acceptable changes in side play, closing force, lid alignment, magnet retention, cracking, squeak, coating wear and charging behavior. The test record should identify the case version, cycle speed, opening angle and inspection intervals.

faq: What should a buyer ask an earbuds charging-case hinge factory?
Ask about hinge structure, lid gap, alignment, opening and closing force, magnet feel, cycle testing, rejection criteria and changes after custom finishing.
Does every visible hinge gap mean the charging case is defective?
Not necessarily. Some functional clearance may support smooth movement, so the buyer should define allowable appearance and functional limits for the selected structure.
Can custom coating affect charging-case lid feel?
A finish can change friction, reveal rubbing or alter visible split lines, so the final coated sample should be reviewed with the approved hinge and magnets.
